title: The AI memory shortage reached your phone bill, so T-Mobile will let you pay it off slower
excerpt: T-Mobile will finance your phone's taxes and fees over 36 months for $0 down, blaming the AI-driven memory shortage for rising phone prices.
content_html:
The AI memory shortage has reached the phone-shop counter. T-Mobile is rolling out financing that lets customers walk out with a new handset for nothing down. It does this by spreading not just the device but its taxes and fees over three years. The reason its executives give is unusually blunt: chips are getting dearer, and phones with them.

The plan, EIP Flex 36, launches on Thursday. It rolls the phone, the taxes and the fees into 36 monthly payments, with nothing due at checkout. The pitch is that even “zero down” deals still make you hand over $100 or more in taxes and fees on the way out. T-Mobile says it is the only plan in wireless to fold those in.

Why phones cost more

The interesting part is the why, and T-Mobile does not hide it. Its executives blame the memory shortage. Chief executive Srini Gopalan told investors that memory-price increases are “resulting in higher prices for smartphones across the board,” a trend he expects to continue. His marketing chief, Andre Almeida, said taxes and fees have climbed with the phones, driven by demand for chips and memory.

That demand is the AI boom. The same scramble for memory that is filling data centres has pushed up the price of the chips inside everyday electronics. Apple has raised prices, AMD marked up graphics cards, and Fujifilm put up its cameras. Microsoft is even slimming Windows to fit machines with less RAM. Now the bill has landed at the carrier.

The catch

The offer is narrower than it sounds. The nothing-down price and the 0% interest apply only to “well-qualified customers.” The fine print puts the rate anywhere from 0% to 24%, depending on credit. Stretching payments to 36 months, up from 24, also ties customers to the carrier for longer.

It fits a wider pattern. Financing and leasing schemes have spread across the industry for the same reason: devices are getting too expensive to buy outright. T-Mobile also rebranded its unlimited plans as “2.0” versions, though the features and prices are unchanged. It is a formality to pair with the new financing, as CNET noted. It added student plans from $30 a month too.

T-Mobile is the second-biggest US carrier, and under Gopalan it is chasing Verizon for the top. Rivals are cutting prices as well, so a slicker way to pay is a competitive weapon.

But the subtext of the day is bigger than one promotion. The cost of the AI build-out is working its way down to what you pay for a phone, and T-Mobile’s answer is to let you pay for it more slowly.

content_html_zh:
AI内存短缺已经到了手机店柜台。 T-Mobile 正在推出融资服务，让客户可以免费购买新手机。 为此，它不仅将设备分摊，还将其税费分摊到三年内。 该公司高管给出的理由异常直白：芯片越来越贵，手机也越来越贵。

该计划名为 EIP Flex 36，于周四推出。 它将电话费、税费和费用分为 36 个月付款，结帐时无需支付任何费用。 其宣传内容是，即使是“零首付”交易，您在退出时仍需缴纳 100 美元或更多的税费。 T-Mobile 表示，这是无线领域唯一将这些功能纳入其中的计划。

为什么手机成本更高

有趣的是原因，T-Mobile 并没有隐藏它。 其高管将其归咎于内存短缺。 首席执行官 Srini Gopalan 告诉投资者，内存价格上涨“导致智能手机价格全面上涨”，他预计这一趋势将持续下去。 他的营销主管安德烈·阿尔梅达 (Andre Almeida) 表示，在芯片和内存需求的推动下，税费随着手机的推出而上涨。

这种需求就是人工智能的繁荣。 数据中心对内存的争夺也推高了日常电子产品中芯片的价格。 苹果提高了价格，AMD提高了显卡价格，富士胶片提高了相机价格。 微软甚至正在精简Windows以适应内存较少的机器。 现在账单已到达承运人处。

陷阱

这个报价比听起来要窄。 无首付价格和 0% 利息仅适用于“合格客户”。 细则将利率定在 0% 到 24% 之间，具体取决于信用情况。 将付款期限从 24 个月延长至 36 个月，也可以使客户与运营商的联系更长久。

它适合更广泛的模式。 出于同样的原因，融资和租赁计划已遍布整个行业：设备变得太昂贵而无法直接购买。 T-Mobile 还将其无限套餐重新命名为“2.0”版本，但功能和价格保持不变。 正如 CNET 指出的那样，这是与新融资配合的一种形式。 它还增加了学生计划，每月 30 美元起。

T-Mobile 是美国第二大运营商，在 Gopalan 的领导下，它正在追赶 Verizon 的榜首。 竞争对手也在降价，因此更灵活的支付方式是一种竞争武器。

但这一天的潜台词不仅仅是一次促销活动。 人工智能构建的成本正在逐渐降低到你购买手机的成本，而 T-Mobile 的答案是让你更慢地支付费用。
